name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Press
description: The single-arm dumbbell press is a unilateral pressing exercise performed lying on a bench with one dumbbell at a time. Because only one side is loaded, the core and obliques must work hard to prevent the torso from rotating, adding a significant anti-rotation stability demand on top of the standard pectoralis and triceps pressing stimulus.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a flat bench holding a single dumbbell in one hand at chest level. The opposite arm can rest on the torso or be held out for balance. Feet are flat on the floor.
execution.setup_instructions: Select a dumbbell lighter than you would use for a bilateral press. Lie on a flat bench and position the dumbbell at chest level before beginning.
steps: Step 1: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in one hand, elbow bent and arm at chest level.
Step 2: Brace the core firmly to resist the uneven loading.
Step 3: Exhale and press the dumbbell straight up until the arm is extended above the chest.
Step 4: Inhale and lower the dumbbell slowly back to the chest level. Complete all reps, then switch arms.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the press; inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Allowing the torso to rotate toward the working side — resist this with core tension
Using a weight so heavy that the shoulder rolls off the bench
safety_considerations: Keep both shoulder blades in contact with the bench throughout the movement
Start with a conservative weight to gauge the anti-rotation demand
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower to chest level for a full stretch, press to full arm extension.
coaching_cues: Resist the urge to rotate — keep both shoulders pinned to the bench
Brace as if you are about to take a punch to the torso
